player_intent: Equipping either the AK-47 or M4A1 in the real game uses its measured AGLS model and sockets while retaining the accepted SOCOM two-hand aim, square-shoulder fire recovery, stable left-palm contact, authored prone firing pose, and human reload presentation.
acceptance_rule: AK-47 and M4A1 load through res://main.tscn with their exact AGLS model and seven authored sockets. The trigger hand remains the sole weapon-root owner, only the support hand may solve to the foregrip, accepted standing and crouched shots use the shared authored recovery for 1.2 seconds, and weapon swaps reconfigure one existing contact modifier instead of appending nodes. The AK-47 saved profile remains authoritative in prone: hand_socket_ik_enabled is false, support_hand_socket_ik_enabled is true, right_hand_owns_weapon is true, relaxed prone resolves to RELAXED_RIFLE_LOCOMOTION, and relaxed-prone plus prone-fire samples keep right-hand IK stopped and the weapon on its authored trigger-hand mount. The verified AK reload may replace the generic standing/crouched reload; the rejected AGLS hold-pose strips and unsafe M4A4 reload may not enter canonical routing. Ballistics, reticle, camera, movement, and networking do not change.

nodes.role: Acts as the shared asset class for two-hand rifles: weapon assets inherit stable standing/crouched FIRE_RECOVERY presentation while retaining only model, socket, ballistics, and verified reload overrides.
Instantiates the equipped AGLS weapon under the canonical operator and publishes its physical socket nodes to presentation consumers.

Consumes already-authorized AK/M4 profiles, rebuilds the shared animation graph, rebinds the weapon presentation owners, and reconfigures the existing contact modifier without granting gameplay equipment.
Resolves the equipped weapon's verified reload slot at the canonical presentation consumer while leaving the shared reload transaction and timing owner unchanged.

must_not_change: CharacterBody3D movement, posture, and collision authority
SOCOM camera and reticle aim authority or accepted reticle geometry
server shot validation, muzzle, ballistics, damage, and networking authority
right trigger-hand attachment as sole weapon-root transform owner
unrelated weapon profiles and user-authored dirty worktree changes

system_delta.reason: Merge measured AGLS AK/M4 models, physical sockets, canonical equipment routing, the human AK reload, and published M4 profile parity into the accepted shared rifle presentation. Keep TWO_HAND_RIFLE as the single family default for stable standing/crouched FIRE_RECOVERY. Replace the unconditional prone READY_SOLVER/full-arm override with the saved AK support-only profile so the authored prone trigger arm and hand-owned weapon mount remain intact. Replace repeated contact-modifier binding with in-place reconfiguration. Reject AGLS hold-pose strips and the M4A4 reload because rendered evidence shows unstable hand contacts and nonhuman torso/shoulder motion.

current.system: Measured rifle presentation with an unconditional prone READY_SOLVER override that can ignore the AK-47 support-only profile

candidate.system: Canonical measured AK/M4 presentation using one shared human rifle pose pipeline, bounded support-hand contact, and saved-profile authority in prone

visual_check: Launch res://main.tscn, equip AK-47 and then M4A1, and inspect standing, crouched, and prone idle, movement, one accepted shot plus its full 1.2-second recovery, and reload. Each exact weapon model must remain attached to the right trigger hand, its left palm must remain on the authored foregrip, shoulders must retain the authored recovery silhouette while the torso aims toward the reticle, and no equip cycle may add another contact modifier. In AK-47 prone idle and fire, confirm the authored trigger arm does not invert or rise above the head and only the support arm closes onto the handguard. The M4 must keep the generic human reload; the AK may use only its verified AGLS reload.
